about: The federal officeholder's day (OFFICE-FEDERAL): every number the federal day reads. Read by src/core2/office-day-federal.ts.

whipAnswerCloseness.source: How far a member's answer to their party's whip moves the closeness between them, a yes warming it and a no cooling it, against the step one ordinary contact gives (a canvass at the door moves it 0.1). Whips keep long memories, but one answer is one exchange (Evans 2018, 'The Whips: Building Party Coalitions in Congress').

cabinetQualificationYears.source: Years in public office at which a cabinet nominee counts as fully qualified for the appointments engine (qualification 0 to 1, rising evenly). Cabinet secretaries since 1980 averaged roughly a decade in prior federal, state or local office (Cohen 1988, 'The Politics of the U.S. Cabinet'; Partnership for Public Service nominee tracker).

budgetRequestShift.source: How far the president's budget request moves a line from the enacted level when they want it moved with full force, as a share of the line. Requests usually move a function's outlays a few percent against the prior enacted year (OMB, Historical Tables, table 3.2 against the President's Budget requests, FY2015 to FY2025).

secretaryBudgetWeight.source: How much a confirmed secretary's own view of their department's line counts in the president's request, against the president's own view (weight 1): departments propose and OMB and the president decide (31 U.S.C. sec. 1108; Wildavsky 1964, 'The Politics of the Budgetary Process').

addressWeight.source: How far one televised address moves a viewer's impression of the president, against a face-to-face town hall's weight in the meetings engine; televised addresses move opinion little and briefly (Edwards 2003, 'On Deaf Ears: The Limits of the Bully Pulpit').

nominationCloseness.source: How far a nomination moves the closeness between the president and the nominee (and a rejection by the Senate cools nothing between them), against the step one ordinary contact gives (0.1).

peopleMetOnTrip.source: How many people a president or member meets face to face at a stop on a trip to a town (a rope line, a diner, a small business), counting only the conversations long enough to remember; staged visits put a handful of residents with the official for more than a handshake.

tripMeetingHours.source: Hours a traveler spends with each person met at a stop, the first tie's time together for the core's meeting record.

tripImpressionWeight.source: How far a face-to-face meeting on a trip moves the person's impression of the traveler, against the meetings engine's town hall weight; a personal meeting with a president or member leaves a strong impression on the few who have one.

confirmationSittingDays.source: Senate sitting days from a cabinet nomination to its confirmation vote. The 2025 cabinet's votes ran from January 20 (Secretary of State, the day of the inauguration) to March 10 (Secretary of Labor), most in the first three weeks of February; the median nominee waited about ten sitting days (Senate roll call votes, 119th Congress, first session). Nominations later in a term wait longer for their hearings.

filingActHours.source: A candidate's own filing for re-election at the clerk, registrar or board of elections: about an hour to complete and submit the declaration and petitions already gathered (state election offices' published candidate filing procedures).

holdMinute.source: The minute of the morning (8 a.m.) at which the day's floor vote, the whip's ask, a vacant cabinet post or a duty due that day holds the player, before the House convenes (it usually meets at noon or 10 a.m. on legislative days, House Majority Leader's daily floor schedule).

situationRoomOpenDays.source: How many days a disaster stays on the situation room's list after its incident begins. FEMA incident periods run from a few days (a tornado) to months (a flood or fire season), and most declared incidents open the president's attention for about a month (FEMA OpenFEMA Disaster Declarations Summaries, incident begin and end dates).
